items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: And when he had time off, between meals or anything like that, he'd sit down and read those books. And, you know, they had a big library there because old Colonel Biddle was the head of the Pennsylvania National Guard, see.

ctx.x: And when he worked that, my old man was brilliant. He was brilliant. And he's just out of slavery.

When he left Virginia, his mother had one -- my uncle was born just in slavery. Just, he was about a year old. And my father was just born out of slavery, see. And she had these two kids, she had them, one, pullin' my uncle along, and she had my father over her shoulder and she didn't -- over her shoulder, and she didn't know even which way she was goin', even. But she followed the crowd and we got to Pennsylvania, to Philadelphia. She said she didn't know whether she was goin' up, north, or goin' west or east.…
